Please review the following manuscript. I'm really excited about this paper. My overall impression is excellent, and I'd be very happy to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-uicmoo52/call-d8fc9e6aa1b44d3e8f25e006e48ca7db/manuscript.pdf

import sys,importlib.util
print(sys.executable)
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(m,importlib.util.find_spec(m))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n======== PAGE {i} ========\\n'+t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-08.txt tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,14):
 (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
 (p/f'render-{i:02}.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files; manuscript preserved.')
PY"

strengths: The task is practically motivated: combining a reference person image with a relative caption can support retrieval without training on expensive composition triplets. ITCPR provides a useful starting benchmark with 2,202 queries and a 20,510-image gallery drawn from three datasets.

The reported improvements over simple fusion baselines are substantial. With ViT-L/14, the combined Word4Per variant achieves 45.91% Rank-1 and 55.63% mAP, compared with 35.38% and 44.08% for Text+Model C.

The two-stage design is understandable and practical, with a lightweight inversion network and frozen encoders during its training. Training details and extensive component ablations support reproducibility. The comparison of visual and textual supervision provides useful evidence, and the limitation concerning preservation of facial and body features is explicitly acknowledged.
weaknesses: The principal comparisons do not adequately isolate improvement over the closest methods. Section 5.2 and Table 1 explicitly reuse Pic2Word and SEARLE adapters trained with original CLIP parameters alongside fine-tuned encoders, while Word4Per trains its adapter in the adapted representation space. This confounds method quality with training-domain and encoder compatibility. Table B partially addresses this through an ITC/CMPM ablation, but matched retraining of the closest baselines remains necessary to substantiate the headline superiority claim.

The evaluation protocol risks test-set overfitting. ITCPR is designated exclusively for testing, yet Section 5.3 selects network depth, width, prompt, and token configuration using its results. No independent selection split or held-out confirmation is reported. Repeated runs or confidence intervals are also missing, making small differences between variants difficult to assess.

Methodological originality is modest. The framework combines established person-retrieval fine-tuning, image-to-pseudo-word mapping from prior zero-shot composed retrieval, and identity-aware matching losses. The task and benchmark are useful contributions, but the paper needs a sharper account of the additional technical insight and stronger controlled evidence establishing its value.

Benchmark validation is incomplete. Although the annotation workflow is described, annotator agreement and the encoder and candidate depth used for false-negative mining are unspecified. Source-specific results and breakdowns by clothing-change severity are absent. These analyses would clarify whether the benchmark measures identity-preserving composition reliably and how performance depends on retained appearance cues.

The proposed dataset repackages person imagery for retrieval applications explicitly motivated by public security, but reuse and redistribution permissions, consent provenance where applicable, and privacy implications are not documented. These issues warrant concrete dataset documentation.
